metadata.title: On Model Selection Consistency of Lasso
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: Lasso Estimator
nodes.statement: $\hat{\beta}^n(\lambda) = \arg\min_\beta \|Y^n - X^n \beta\|_2^2 + \lambda \|\beta\|_1$, an $L_1$-regularized least squares estimator that yields sparse coefficients.
nodes.statement_clean: The Lasso minimizes squared loss plus an L1 penalty on the coefficients.

nodes.name: Linear Regression Model
nodes.statement: Data are generated by $Y^n = X^n \beta^n + \varepsilon^n$, where $\varepsilon^n = (\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_n)^T$ are i.i.d. with mean $0$ and variance $\sigma^2$, $X^n$ is the $n \times p$ design matrix, and $\beta^n$ is sparse with $q$ nonzero entries.
nodes.statement_clean: Standard sparse linear regression with i.i.d. zero-mean noise; only $q$ of $p$ coefficients are nonzero.

nodes.name: Sign Equality (=_s)
nodes.statement: An estimate $\hat{\beta}^n$ is equal in sign with $\beta^n$, written $\hat{\beta}^n =_s \beta^n$, iff $\mathrm{sign}(\hat{\beta}^n) = \mathrm{sign}(\beta^n)$, where $\mathrm{sign}(\cdot)$ maps positives to $1$, negatives to $-1$, and zero to zero.
nodes.statement_clean: Sign equality matches signs entry-wise (and zeros to zeros) between estimate and truth.

nodes.name: Strong Sign Consistency
nodes.statement: Lasso is Strongly Sign Consistent if there exists a deterministic $\lambda_n = f(n)$ (independent of $Y^n, X^n$) such that $\lim_{n\to\infty} P(\hat{\beta}^n(\lambda_n) =_s \beta^n) = 1$.
nodes.statement_clean: Some preselected $\lambda_n$ recovers the true sign pattern asymptotically with probability one.

nodes.name: General Sign Consistency
nodes.statement: Lasso is General Sign Consistent if $\lim_{n\to\infty} P(\exists \lambda \geq 0,\ \hat{\beta}^n(\lambda) =_s \beta^n) = 1$.
nodes.statement_clean: For each draw, some data-dependent $\lambda$ on the path recovers the sign pattern.

nodes.name: Design Block Decomposition
nodes.statement: With $\beta^n = (\beta^n_{(1)}, \beta^n_{(2)})$ ordered so the first $q$ entries are nonzero, write $C^n = \frac{1}{n}(X^n)^T X^n$ in blocks $C^n_{11}, C^n_{12}, C^n_{21}, C^n_{22}$ corresponding to relevant/irrelevant covariates.
nodes.statement_clean: Partition the Gram matrix $C^n$ into relevant-vs-irrelevant blocks.

nodes.name: Strong Irrepresentable Condition
nodes.statement: There exists a positive constant vector $\eta$ such that $|C^n_{21}(C^n_{11})^{-1}\mathrm{sign}(\beta^n_{(1)})| \leq 1 - \eta$, where the inequality is element-wise and $1$ is a $(p-q)\times 1$ vector of ones.
nodes.statement_clean: Irrelevant covariates are uniformly not representable (with margin $\eta$) by relevant ones in the sign-weighted regression sense.

nodes.name: Weak Irrepresentable Condition
nodes.statement: $|C^n_{21}(C^n_{11})^{-1}\mathrm{sign}(\beta^n_{(1)})| < 1$, with strict element-wise inequality but no uniform margin.
nodes.statement_clean: Strict but margin-free version of the Irrepresentable Condition.

nodes.name: Lower Bound on Sign-Recovery Probability
nodes.statement: Assume Strong Irrepresentable Condition holds with $\eta > 0$. Then $P(\hat{\beta}^n(\lambda_n) =_s \beta^n) \geq P(A_n \cap B_n)$, where $A_n$ and $B_n$ are events controlling the sign of $\hat{\beta}^n_{(1)}$ and the shrinkage of $\hat{\beta}^n_{(2)}$ to zero.
nodes.statement_clean: Sign-recovery probability is bounded below by the joint probability of two noise-controlled events depending on $\lambda_n$ and $\eta$.
assumptions: Strong Irrepresentable Condition holds with constant $\eta > 0$

nodes.name: Strong Sign Consistency for Fixed $p$
nodes.statement: For fixed $q, p$, $\beta^n = \beta$, under regularity conditions (3) and (4), if Strong Irrepresentable Condition holds, then for any $\lambda_n$ with $\lambda_n / n \to 0$ and $\lambda_n / n^{(1+c)/2} \to \infty$, $0 \le c < 1$: $P(\hat{\beta}^n(\lambda_n) =_s \beta^n) = 1 - o(e^{-n^c})$.
nodes.statement_clean: In the classical fixed-$p$ regime, the Strong Irrepresentable Condition is sufficient for exponentially fast strong sign consistency.
assumptions: $\lambda_n / n \to 0$ and $\lambda_n / n^{(1+c)/2} \to \infty$ for some $0 \le c < 1$

nodes.name: Necessity of Weak Irrepresentable for General Sign Consistency
nodes.statement: For fixed $p, q, \beta^n = \beta$ under regularity conditions (3) and (4), if Lasso is general sign consistent, then there exists $N$ such that the Weak Irrepresentable Condition holds for all $n > N$.
nodes.statement_clean: General sign consistency forces (eventually) the Weak Irrepresentable Condition.
conclusions: $\exists N$ such that for all $n > N$, $|C^n_{21}(C^n_{11})^{-1}\mathrm{sign}(\beta^n_{(1)})| < 1$ holds element-wise

nodes.name: Strong Sign Consistency for Large $p$
nodes.statement: Assume $\varepsilon^n_i$ i.i.d. with $E(\varepsilon^n_i)^{2k} < \infty$ for integer $k > 0$. Under conditions (5)-(8), Strong Irrepresentable Condition implies strong sign consistency for $p_n = o(n^{(c_2-c_1)k})$. For $\lambda_n / \sqrt{n} = o(n^{(c_2-c_1)/2})$ and $\frac{1}{p_n}(\lambda_n/\sqrt{n})^{2k} \to \infty$: $P(\hat{\beta}^n(\lambda_n) =_s \beta^n) \geq 1 - O(p_n n^k / \lambda_n^{2k}) \to 1$.
nodes.statement_clean: With finite $2k$th noise moments, the Strong Irrepresentable Condition gives strong sign consistency at polynomial rates of $p_n$.

nodes.name: Strong Sign Consistency for Gaussian Noise
nodes.statement: Assume $\varepsilon^n_i$ i.i.d. Gaussian. Under conditions (5)-(8), if there exists $0 \leq c_3 < c_2 - c_1$ with $p_n = O(e^{n^{c_3}})$, then Strong Irrepresentable Condition implies strong sign consistency. For $\lambda_n \propto n^{(1+c_4)/2}$ with $c_3 < c_4 < c_2 - c_1$: $P(\hat{\beta}^n(\lambda_n) =_s \beta^n) \geq 1 - o(e^{-n^{c_3}}) \to 1$.
nodes.statement_clean: Under Gaussian noise, dimension $p_n$ may grow exponentially in $n$ while sign consistency holds at exponential rate.

nodes.name: Regularity Conditions for Fixed $p$
nodes.statement: $C^n \to C$ as $n \to \infty$ with $C$ positive definite (eq. (3)); and $\frac{1}{n}\max_{1 \leq i \leq n}(x^n_i)^T x^n_i \to 0$ (eq. (4)).

nodes.name: Regularity Conditions for Large $p$
nodes.statement: There exist $0 \le c_1 < c_2 \le 1$ and $M_1, M_2, M_3, M_4 > 0$ such that: (5) $\frac{1}{n}(X^n_i)^T X^n_i \le M_1$ for all $i$; (6) $\alpha^T C^n_{11} \alpha \geq M_2$ for all $\|\alpha\|_2 = 1$; (7) $q_n = O(n^{c_1})$; (8) $n^{(1-c_2)/2}\min_{i=1,\dots,q}|\beta^n_i| \geq M_3$.

nodes.name: KKT Characterization of Lasso Solutions
nodes.statement: $\hat{\beta}^n(\lambda) = (\hat{\beta}^n_1,\dots)$ is a Lasso solution iff $\frac{d\|Y^n - X^n\beta\|_2^2}{d\beta_j}\big|_{\beta_j=\hat{\beta}^n_j} = \lambda \mathrm{sign}(\hat{\beta}^n_j)$ when $\hat{\beta}^n_j \neq 0$, and $|\frac{d\|Y^n - X^n\beta\|_2^2}{d\beta_j}\big|_{\beta_j=\hat{\beta}^n_j}| \leq \lambda$ when $\hat{\beta}^n_j = 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Direct KKT conditions for the Lasso, characterizing zero vs. nonzero coordinates.

nodes.name: Constant Positive Correlation Design
nodes.statement: Suppose $C^n$ has $1$'s on the diagonal and a common off-diagonal entry $r_n$ with $0 < r_n \leq 1/(1+cq)$ for some $c > 0$. Then Strong Irrepresentable Condition holds.
nodes.statement_clean: Equicorrelated designs with bounded common correlation satisfy Strong Irrepresentable Condition.

nodes.name: Bounded Correlation Design
nodes.statement: If $\beta$ has $q$ nonzero entries, $C^n$ has $1$'s on the diagonal, and $|r_{ij}| \leq c/(2q-1)$ for some $0 \leq c < 1$, then Strong Irrepresentable Condition holds.
nodes.statement_clean: Slightly correlated designs (bound shrinks with $q$) satisfy Strong Irrepresentable Condition.

nodes.name: Power Decay Correlation Design
nodes.statement: If $C^n_{ij} = (\rho_n)^{|i-j|}$ for all $i, j$, with $|\rho_n| \leq c < 1$, then Strong Irrepresentable Condition holds for any $q$.
nodes.statement_clean: AR(1)-style power-decay correlation always satisfies Strong Irrepresentable Condition.
conclusions: Strong Irrepresentable Condition holds for any $q$

nodes.name: Special Designs Satisfying SIC
nodes.statement: Strong Irrepresentable Condition holds if (a) the design is orthogonal, or (b) $q = 1$ with predictors normalized and correlations bounded from $1$, or (c) $p = 2$ with predictors normalized and correlations bounded from $1$.
nodes.statement_clean: Orthogonal, $q=1$, and $p=2$ designs trivially satisfy Strong Irrepresentable Condition.

nodes.name: Block-Wise Design
nodes.statement: For block-diagonal $C^n = \mathrm{diag}(B^n_1,\dots,B^n_k)$ with $\beta^n = (b^n_1,\dots,b^n_k)$ partitioned by blocks, Strong Irrepresentable Condition holds iff there exists a common $0 < \eta \leq 1$ such that it holds for all $(B^n_j, b^n_j)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Block-diagonal designs reduce SIC to per-block conditions with a common margin.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 1
nodes.statement: Reformulate Lasso as $\hat{u}^n = \arg\min V_n(u)$ with $V_n$ differentiable in the smooth part; apply Lemma 1 (KKT) to obtain block equations involving $C^n_{11}, C^n_{21}, W^n$; bound the resulting absolute-value inequalities to recover events $A_n$ and $B_n$.
nodes.statement_clean: Reduces to KKT-induced inequalities that exactly match the events $A_n$ and $B_n$.

nodes.name: Reparametrize via $\hat{u}^n = \hat{\beta}^n - \beta^n$
nodes.statement: Define $\hat{u}^n = \hat{\beta}^n - \beta^n$ and $V_n(u) = \sum_{i=1}^n[(\varepsilon_i - X_i u)^2 - \varepsilon_i^2] + \lambda_n\|u + \beta\|_1$, so $\hat{u}^n = \arg\min_u V_n(u)$.

nodes.name: Simplify smooth part using $C^n$ and $W^n$
nodes.statement: $\sum_i[(\varepsilon_i - X_i u^n)^2 - \varepsilon_i^2] = -2 W^n(\sqrt{n} u^n) + (\sqrt{n} u^n)^T C^n (\sqrt{n} u^n)$ with $W^n = (X^n)^T \varepsilon^n / \sqrt{n}$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 1 (KKT) on blocks
nodes.statement: Using KKT and uniqueness of Lasso, derive $C^n_{11}(\sqrt{n}\hat{u}^n(1)) - W^n(1) = -\frac{\lambda_n}{2\sqrt{n}}\mathrm{sign}(\beta^n_{(1)})$ and $|C^n_{21}(\sqrt{n}\hat{u}^n(1)) - W^n(2)| \leq \frac{\lambda_n}{2\sqrt{n}}1$.

nodes.name: Bound to obtain events $A_n$ and $B_n$
nodes.statement: Substituting and bounding absolute values yields exactly $A_n$ and $B_n$, completing the proof.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement: Apply Proposition 1 and bound $1 - P(A_n \cap B_n)$ by Gaussian tail bounds on the asymptotically normal $z^n_i$ and $\zeta^n_i$ components, using the regularity conditions and the rates on $\lambda_n$.

nodes.name: Invoke Proposition 1 lower bound
nodes.statement: By Proposition 1, $P(\hat{\beta}^n =_s \beta) \geq P(A_n \cap B_n)$, so it suffices to upper bound $P(A_n^c) + P(B_n^c)$.

nodes.name: Apply Gaussian tail bound
nodes.statement: Using $1 - \Phi(t) < t^{-1} e^{-t^2/2}$ and the assumed rates on $\lambda_n$, both $\sum_q P(|z^n_i|\geq\dots) = o(e^{-n^c})$ and $\sum_{p-q} P(|\zeta^n_i|\geq\dots) = o(e^{-n^c})$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: Argue by contradiction: if Weak Irrepresentable Condition fails infinitely often, an asymptotically normal coordinate of $C^n_{21}(C^n_{11})^{-1} W^n(1) - W^n(2)$ has non-vanishing probability of taking the wrong sign, contradicting general sign consistency.

nodes.name: Define event $F_1^n$ and reduce via Lemma 1
nodes.statement: On $F_1^n$ where some $\lambda_n$ achieves correct signs, KKT yields the same block equations as in Proposition 1's proof, giving $F_1^n \subset F_2^n$ where $F_2^n$ involves intervals $[(\lambda_n/2\sqrt{n})L^n, (\lambda_n/2\sqrt{n})U^n]$ with $L^n, U^n$ depending on $\mathrm{sign}(\beta^n_{(1)})$.

nodes.name: Contradiction from non-vanishing tail
nodes.statement: If WIC fails so some entry of $|C^n_{21}(C^n_{11})^{-1}\mathrm{sign}(\beta^n_{(1)})| \geq 1$, then the centered Gaussian limit assigns positive probability to the wrong sign for that entry, forcing $\liminf P(F_1^n) < 1$, contradicting general sign consistency.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorems 3 and 4
nodes.statement: Following the structure of Theorem 1's proof, decompose $z^n_i = (h_a^i)^T \varepsilon$ and $\zeta^n_i = (h_b^i)^T \varepsilon$ with $\|h_a^i\|_2^2 \leq 1/M_2$, $\|h_b^i\|_2^2 \leq M_1$; then bound tail probabilities using either bounded-moment Markov bounds (Theorem 3) or Gaussian tails (Theorem 4).

nodes.name: Express $z^n_i, \zeta^n_i$ as inner products $(h\cdot)^T \varepsilon$
nodes.statement: Write $H_A^T = (C^n_{11})^{-1}(n^{-1/2} X^n(1)^T)$ giving $H_A^T H_A = (C^n_{11})^{-1}$; analogously $H_B^T H_B$ has spectrum bounded by $M_1$. Hence $\|h_a^i\|^2 \leq 1/M_2$ and $\|h_b^i\|^2 \leq M_1$.

nodes.name: Bounded moments tail bound (Theorem 3)
nodes.statement: $E(\alpha^T \varepsilon^n)^{2k} \leq (2k-1)!! \|\alpha\|_2^2 E(\varepsilon^n_i)^{2k}$, so $P(z^n_i > t) = O(t^{-2k})$, giving $\sum_q P(|z^n_i|>\dots) + \sum_{p-q} P(|\zeta^n_i|>\dots) = O(p_n n^k / \lambda_n^{2k})$.

nodes.name: Gaussian-noise tail bound (Theorem 4)
nodes.statement: When $\varepsilon_i$ Gaussian, $z_i, \zeta_i$ are Gaussian; using $1 - \Phi(t) < t^{-1} e^{-t^2/2}$ with $\lambda_n \propto n^{(1+c_4)/2}$, tail sums are $o(e^{-n^{c_3}})$.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 1
nodes.statement: Use the closed-form inverse for an equicorrelated matrix (eigenvalues $a + (q-1)b$ and $a - b$) to compute $C^n_{21}(C^n_{11})^{-1}$ explicitly; bound $|C^n_{21}(C^n_{11})^{-1}\mathrm{sign}(\beta^n_{(1)})| \leq qr_n/(1+(q-1)r_n) \leq 1/(1+c)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 2
nodes.statement: Bound $|\alpha^T (C^n_{11})^{-1}\mathrm{sign}(\beta^n_{(1)})|$ by $\|\alpha\| \|\mathrm{sign}\|/e_1$; show $e_1 \geq q/(2q-1)$ via Cauchy-Schwartz, giving the result $|C^n_{21}(C^n_{11})^{-1}\mathrm{sign}(\beta^n_{(1)})| < c\,1$.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 3
nodes.statement: Reduce the power-decay (AR(1)) design to its Markov-chain structure so $x_{jk} \perp x_{jg} | (x_{jk_l}, x_{jk_h})$; reduce SIC to a 2-by-2 regression and compute the sum of regression coefficients $1 - (1-\rho^{k_l-k})(1-\rho^{k-k_h})/(1+\rho^{k_l-k_h}) < 1 - (1-c)^2/2$.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 4
nodes.statement: (a) Orthogonal $\Rightarrow$ Corollary 2 applies. (b) $q=1 \Rightarrow 1/(2q-1) = 1$, Corollary 2 applies. (c) $p=2$: trivial for $q\in\{0,2\}$, otherwise reduces to (b).

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 5
nodes.statement: $C^n_{21}(C^n_{11})^{-1}\mathrm{sign}(\beta^n_{(1)})$ decomposes block-diagonally into $C^n_{M^c \cap B_j, M \cap B_j}(C^n_{M \cap B_j, M \cap B_j})^{-1}\mathrm{sign}(\beta^n_{M \cap B_j})$, so SIC is equivalent to its per-block version with a common margin.

nodes.name: Simulation 1: 3-Variable (In)Consistency Example
nodes.statement: With $x_{i1}, x_{i2}, e_i, \varepsilon_i$ i.i.d. variance $1$ mean $0$, $x_{i3} = \frac{2}{3}x_{i1} + \frac{2}{3}x_{i2} + \frac{1}{3}e_i$, $Y_i = x_{i1}\beta_1 + x_{i2}\beta_2 + \varepsilon_i$. Setting (a) $\beta_1 = 2, \beta_2 = 3$ fails SIC; setting (b) $\beta_1 = -2, \beta_2 = 3$ satisfies SIC.
nodes.statement_clean: A 3-predictor toy example where Lasso is inconsistent under (a) and consistent under (b).

nodes.name: Simulation 2: Quantitative Relation between SIC margin $\eta_\infty$ and Selection Probability
nodes.statement: $n=100, p=32, q=5, \beta_{(1)} = (7,4,2,1,1)^T, \sigma^2 = 0.1$. Generate $100$ designs from Wishart$(p,p)$, run $1000$ Lasso paths each, plot selection rate vs $\eta_\infty = 1 - \|C^n_{21}(C^n_{11})^{-1}\mathrm{sign}(\beta^n_{(1)})\|_\infty$.
nodes.statement_clean: Empirically, sign-recovery rate transitions sharply around $\eta_\infty = 0$, validating Proposition 1 / Theorems 1-4.

nodes.name: Simulation 3: How Often SIC Holds Under Wishart Designs
nodes.statement: For $p \in \{2^3,\dots,2^8\}$ and $q \in \{p/8, 2p/8, \dots, 7p/8\}$, sample $1000$ $C^n$ from Wishart$(p,p)$ (rescaled to unit diagonal) and compute the proportion satisfying SIC. Reported in Table 1.
nodes.statement_clean: SIC holds frequently for very sparse models but rarely for moderate $q/p$ ratios.

nodes.name: Coherence Connection (Donoho et al. 2004)
nodes.statement: Corollary 2's bound $\max_{i,j}|C^n_{ij}| < 1/(2q-1)$ coincides with the Coherence condition for sparsest-estimate $L_2$ recovery in Donoho et al. (2004); for Lasso, Donoho et al. require the tighter $\max_{i,j}|C^n_{ij}| < 1/(4q-1)$.

nodes.name: Comparison with Thresholding
nodes.statement: Hard/soft thresholding of OLS with $t_n/\sqrt{n} \to \infty$ and $t_n \to 0$ gives consistent selection in the small-$p$ regime; however, OLS is undefined for $p > n$, while Lasso (Theorems 3, 4) handles $p \gg n$.

nodes.name: Knight-Fu Estimation Consistency for Lasso (cited)
nodes.statement: For fixed $p$ and $\beta^n = \beta$, if $\lambda_n = o(n)$ then $\hat{\beta}^n(\lambda_n) \to_p \beta$ and the estimates are asymptotically normal.
nodes.origin_citation: Knight and Fu, Annals of Statistics 28 (2000)

nodes.name: LARS / Lasso Path Algorithm (cited)
nodes.statement: Computes the entire Lasso regularization path in the complexity of one linear regression by following the least-angle direction.
